claim: Pancreatic cancer is the deadliest major cancer.
source: Pancreatic cancer is the deadliest major cancer (Siegel et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Siegel et al., 2020

claim: The tumor microenvironment, composed of a dense fibroinflammatory stroma, contributes to the difficulty in treating pancreatic cancer.

claim: TAM abundance correlates with worse response to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma therapy.

claim: TAMs promote cancer cell proliferation and metastasis.

evidence: Supported by citation to Qian and Pollard, 2010

claim: TAMs have been linked to promoting chemoresistance.
source: TAMs have also been linked to promoting chemoresistance (Zhu et al., 2014)

claim: TAMs have long been considered anti-inflammatory 'M2-like' macrophages.

claim: Overlap exists between the phenotypes of M2 and TAMs, including oxidative metabolism and immunosuppressive properties such as the expression of Arginase-1.

claim: The diverse molecular stimuli found throughout the TME polarize TAMs into macrophages with properties not shared with other classical subtypes.

claim: Bone marrow-derived macrophages were polarized in vitro with conditioned media from a PDA cell line in which mutant Kras activity can be regulated.

evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study

claim: Macrophages polarized with PDA cell-conditioned media are referred to as tumor-educated macrophages (TEMs) to distinguish them from TAMs arising in a tumor.
source: We refer to macrophages polarized under these conditions as tumor-educated macrophages (TEMs) to distinguish them from TAMs arising in a tumor.
evidence: This is a definitional statement made by the authors

claim: A systems biology approach integrating multiomic profiling (transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics) was used to define biomarkers for and properties of TEMs.
source: We then utilized a systems biology approach integrating our multiomic profiling (i.e., transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics) to define biomarkers for, and the properties of, TEMs.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach used in the study

claim: Contrasting TEM data with data from proinflammatory 'M1-like' and 'M2-like' macrophages revealed markers and pathways that illustrate distinct functional characteristics of TEMs relative to classical subtypes.

claim: In-house single-cell RNA sequencing datasets verified the expression of several TEM markers in human pancreatic TAMs.

claim: Cancer cell mutant Kras activity plays an important role in TEM polarization through GM-CSF and lactate.

claim: GM-CSF instructs TEM gene expression and metabolism through the PI3K–AKT pathway.

claim: Fresh media was included at a ratio of one to three parts conditioned media to account for nutrients consumed by the cancer cells.

claim: TAMs are one of the most abundant cell types in PDA and participate in therapeutic resistance through a variety of mechanisms.
source: TAMs are one of the most abundant cell types in PDA and participate in therapeutic resistance through a variety of mechanisms, including resistance to chemotherapy, immunosuppression, and promotion of tumor growth.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on established knowledge

claim: Bulk RNA sequencing, MS-based proteomics, and LC/MS-based metabolomics revealed several distinctions between TEMs and classical macrophage subtypes.
source: Bulk RNA sequencing, MS-based proteomics, and LC/MS-based metabolomics revealed several distinctions between TEMs and classical macrophage subtypes.
evidence: This is a summary of the multiomic analysis results

claim: Txnip, Acly, and Arg1 are unique contributors to TEM metabolism.
source: Our focus on metabolism and cytokine signaling as two primary drivers of cellular function revealed Txnip, Acly, and Arg1 as unique contributors to TEM metabolism.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the multiomic analysis

claim: The top 20 proteins correlated with Txnip showed enrichment in metabolism.
source: The top 20 proteins correlated with Txnip showed enrichment in metabolism.
evidence: This is from the correlation and pathway analysis

claim: Acly revealed strong correlation with Slc25a1, the mitochondrial citrate transporter, along with an increase in citrate abundance with respect to other macrophage subtypes.
source: Acly revealed strong correlation with Slc25a1, the mitochondrial citrate transporter, along with an increase in citrate abundance with respect to other macrophage subtypes, suggesting an important role for this pathway in TEM function.
evidence: This is from the correlation analysis and metabolomics data

claim: Arg1 was strongly correlated with Pik3cd, a catalytic subunit of PI3K, suggesting a role for this pathway in TEM polarization.
source: Arg1 was strongly correlated with Pik3cd, a catalytic subunit of PI3K, suggesting a role for this pathway in TEM polarization.
evidence: This is from the correlation analysis

claim: Expression of several important TEM markers was observed in human TAMs.
source: Next, we queried our in-house scRNA-seq dataset of human tumors, from which we observed expression of several important TEM markers in human TAMs.
evidence: This is from the scRNA-seq analysis of human tumors

claim: Expression of PI3K-related genes in human TAMs indicates persistence of this pathway in macrophage polarization in clinically relevant models.
source: We also note expression of PI3K-related genes in human TAMs, indicating persistence of this pathway in macrophage polarization in clinically relevant models.
evidence: This is an inference from the scRNA-seq data

claim: Proinflammatory markers are not substantially expressed in human TAMs, while anti-inflammatory markers are more abundant.
source: As confirmation of the general understanding of TAMs, we see that proinflammatory markers are not substantially expressed in human TAMs, while anti-inflammatory markers are more abundant.
evidence: This is from the scRNA-seq analysis of human tumors

claim: The most distinct markers of TEM metabolism and cytokine signaling are reliant on Kras expression in PDA cells.
source: Indeed, we observed that the most distinct markers of TEM metabolism and cytokine signaling are reliant on Kras expression in PDA cells.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the Kras-On vs Kras-Off comparison

claim: Kras is known to impact cancer cell glucose metabolism and growth factor expression.
source: Kras is known to impact cancer cell glucose metabolism and growth factor expression.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Kras function

claim: Lactate and GM-CSF are known to be released from cancer cells in greater abundance when mutant Kras is expressed.
source: Specifically, lactate and GM-CSF are known to be released from cancer cells in greater abundance when mutant Kras is expressed.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by previous citations

claim: Several GM-CSF- or lactate-responsive genes are differentially expressed in Kras-On TEMs compared to Kras-Off TEMs.
source: By querying our bulk RNA-seq dataset, we observed several GM-CSF- or lactate-responsive genes differentially expressed in Kras-On TEMs compared to Kras-Off TEMs.
evidence: This is from the RNA-seq analysis

claim: TEM and TAM polarization occurs in response to both metabolic crosstalk and growth factor signaling.
source: These data suggest that TEM and TAM polarization occurs in response to both metabolic crosstalk and growth factor signaling, and build upon previous reports of the role of tumor-derived lactate in TAM polarization (Colegio et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data, supported by citation to Colegio et al., 2014

claim: Both PI3K–AKT inhibition and GM-CSF neutralization reduced Arg1 expression relative to vehicle and IgG control, respectively.
source: In consideration of the GM-CSF–PI3K pathway, and the strong correlation between Arg1 and Pik3cd, we treated BMDMs with either a PI3K inhibitor, AKT inhibitor, or GM-CSF-neutralizing antibody, and observed that both PI3K–AKT inhibition and GM-CSF neutralization reduced Arg1 expression relative to vehicle and IgG control, respectively.
evidence: This is from the Western blot experiments

claim: Changes in TEM metabolism occur in response to GM-CSF neutralization, most notably an increase in citrate, which may potentially be correlated with reduced Acly expression.
source: We also note changes in TEM metabolism in response to GM-CSF neutralization, most notably an increase in citrate, which may potentially be correlated with reduced Acly expression.
evidence: This is from the metabolomics analysis

claim: Mutant Kras exhibits its most significant effects on TEM and TAM polarization through increased release of GM-CSF and lactate from pancreatic cancer cells.
source: Collectively, these data demonstrate an important role for mutant Kras in TEM and TAM polarization, and suggest that mutant Kras exhibits its most significant effects through increased release of GM-CSF and lactate from pancreatic cancer cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data

claim: The epithelial–myeloid axis provides only one node of the complex network of interactions in pancreatic tumors.
source: First, the epithelial–myeloid axis provides only one node of the complex network of interactions in pancreatic tumors.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors

claim: Fibroblasts make up a significant part of the overall cellularity of pancreatic tumors.
source: In particular, fibroblasts make up a significant part of the overall cellularity of pancreatic tumors, and the heterogeneity of fibroblast populations are only now beginning to be understood (Helms et al., 2020; Garcia et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Helms et al., 2020 and Garcia et al., 2020

claim: Many fibroblast populations are noted to be strongly immunosuppressive, potentially providing another source of GM-CSF for the myeloid cells.
source: Among these populations, many are noted to be strongly immunosuppressive, potentially providing another source of GM-CSF for the myeloid cells.
evidence: This is speculation about potential sources of GM-CSF

claim: The pancreatic TME is characterized by poor vasculature.
source: Further, the pancreatic TME is characterized by poor vasculature (Kamphorst et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kamphorst et al., 2015

claim: Future studies will be needed to address the impact of hypoxia and low-nutrient availability on the epithelial–myeloid signaling axis.
source: Future studies will be needed to address the impact of the resulting hypoxia and low-nutrient availability on the epithelial–myeloid signaling axis, features that were not well recapitulated using the cell culture-based approaches presented herein.
evidence: This is a statement about future research needs and limitations of the current study
